Short title extent and commencement

THE PAKISTAN JUNIOR CADET CORPS ACT, 1953
THE PAKISTAN
JUNIOR CADET CORPS ACT, 1953
ACT No. XXXVI of
1953
(For
Statement of Objects and Reasons, see Gaz. of P., 1953, Pt. IX, p. 166.
The Act
has been applied to Baluchistan and in the Federated Areas of Baluchistan, with
effect from the 5th day of November, 1953, see Gaz. of P., 1953, Pt. I, p. 280.
It has

[5th November,
1953]
An Act to constitute a Junior Cadet Corps
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the constitution and maintenance of a Junior Cadet Corps for
Pakistan and for its administration ;
It is hereby enacted as follows :‑
1. Short title extent and
commencement-----‑(1) This Act may be called the Pakistan Junior
Cadet Corps Act, 1953.
(2) It applies to the whole of
Pakistan.
(3) It shall come into force at
once.

Definition

[5th November,
1953]
An Act to constitute a Junior Cadet Corps

provide for the constitution and maintenance of a Junior Cadet Corps for
Pakistan and for its administration ;
2. Definition------In this
Act, unless there is anything repugnant in the subject or context,‑
(a) "cadet" means a
school boy who is deemed to be enrolled as a cadet under sub‑section (1)
of section 5 ;
(b) "Commander‑in‑Chief"
means the Commander‑in -Chief of the Pakistan Army ;
(c) "prescribed" means
prescribed by rules made under this Act.

3. Constitution of Junior
Cadet Corps------There shall be raised and maintained in the manner
hereinafter provided a force, which shall be designated the Junior Cadet Corps,
and shall consist of units constituted under section 4.

Constitution and organization of units

[5th November,
1953]
An Act to constitute a Junior Cadet Corps
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the constitution and maintenance of a Junior Cadet Corps for
Pakistan and for its administration ;
4. Constitution and
organization of units-----‑(1) Subject to the control of the Central
Government, the Commander‑in‑Chief may, by order in writing, direct
the constitution and maintenance for any boys' school in Pakistan of two
separate companies of the Junior Cadet Corps, each company to consist of the
boys of one of each of the two final classes of the school, and may direct the
disbandment of the companies so constituted.
(2) The companies constituted
under sub‑section (1) from schools located in the same revenue district
shall jointly constitute a battalion to be designated after the name of that
district.

Certain students to be deemed to be enrolled

It has
also been extended to the Leased Areas of Baluchistan by the Leased Areas
(Laws) Order, 1950 (G. G. O. 3 of 1950).)
[5th November,
1953]
An Act to constitute a Junior Cadet Corps
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the constitution and maintenance of a Junior Cadet Corps for
Pakistan and for its administration ;
5. Certain students to be
deemed to be enrolled----‑(1) On the constitution of a company under
sub‑section (1) of section 4, every student of the class concerned who,‑
(i) is above thirteen years of
age, at the commencement of the academic year, or by the first day of April of
that year, and
(ii) is certified on examination
by an officer of the Pakis tan Army Medical Corps to be physically fit to
undergo the prescribed military training, shall be deemed to have been enrolled
as a cadet in that company.
(2) A student who is deemed to be enrolled as a cadet in a
company under sub‑section (1) shall not cease to belong to that company,
until he passes out of or otherwise leaves, the class for which the company was
constituted, or is duly certified by an officer of the Pakistan Army Medical
Corps to have become physically unfit to undergo further military training.

An Act to constitute a Junior Cadet Corps
WHEREAS it is expedient to

Pakistan and for its administration ;
6. Officers of the Junior
Cadet Corps------‑(1) The Central Government, on the recommendation
of the Headmaster of the school for which units of the Junior Cadet Corps have
been constituted under sub‑section (1) of sec tion 4, supported by the
Director of Public Instruction of the Province concerned and the officer
commanding the local military formation being not below the rank of brigadier,
may appoint any member of the staff of that school, who is not less than twenty
three and not more than thirty‑five years of age, as an officer of the
corps.
(2) A person appointed officer under sub‑section (1)
shall be granted a commission in the form prescribed in this behalf under sub‑section
(2) of section 232 of the Government of India Act, 1935 (Added by A. O., 1961, Art. 2 and Sch. (with effect from the
23rd March, 1956).)[or under clause (2) of Article 40 of the
Constitution] (Ins. by A. O., 1964, Art. 2 and Sch.)[of
1956 or under clause (2) of Article 17 of the Constitution of 1962]. 26 Geo
5,c.2.

Officers to be attached to regular units for training

[5th November,
1953]
An Act to constitute a Junior Cadet Corps
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the constitution and maintenance of a Junior Cadet Corps for
Pakistan and for its administration ;
7. Officers to be attached to
regular units for training-----An officer of the Junior Cadet Corps shall
be liable, under the orders of the officer commanding the local military
formation being not below the rank of brigadier, to be attached to a unit of
the regular army for undergoing the military training prescribed for his class.

9. Allowance of Officers------An
officer of the Junior Cadet Corps may be paid such allowance by the Provincial
Government concerned as may have been agreed upon between the Central
Government and the Pro vincial Government:
Provided that an officer, who is
attached to a regular unit for training under section 7, shall receive such

10. Termination of officers
commissions------‑(1) The Central Government may withdraw the
commission of an officer at any time and for any cause whatever,
(2) An officer of the Junior
Cadet Corps shall cease to hold his commission,‑
(i) on ceasing to be a member of
the staff of the school from which he received his commission:
Provided that an officer who is
immediately re‑employed in another school for which companies of the
Junior Cadet Corps have been constituted under sub section (1) of section 4
may, on the recommendation of the Headmaster of that school, be allowed by the
Commander‑in‑Chief to retain his commission ;
(ii) on attaining the age of
forty‑five years.

[5th November,
1953]
An Act to constitute a Junior Cadet Corps
WHEREAS it is expedient to
provide for the constitution and maintenance of a Junior Cadet Corps for
Pakistan and for its administration ;
12. Discipline of cadets-----‑(1)
The Headmaster of each school shall be Honorary commanding officer of the
companies constituted for his school under sub‑section (1) of section 4
and the primary responsibility for enforcing discipline in those companies
shall rest on him.
(2) With the approval of the
Commander‑in‑Chief the Headmaster of each school may frame rules
for the punishment of cadets who wilfully and without reasonable cause absent
them selves from parades held for imparting the prescribed military training or
who are otherwise guilty of conduct to the prejudice of good order and
discipline in the Junior Cadet Corps.
(3) In addition to any other
punishment, which the Head master may specify therein, the rules made under sub‑section
(2) shall provide for the subjection of the offender to extra drill for twenty
minutes.

perform service------Officers and cadets of the Junior Cadet Corps shall
not be liable to perform military service of any kind whatever.
